world.crownfall_rule: Crownfall condensed unrealized causal branches into Dawnshards; consuming a shard closes the possibility it contains.
world.future_well_rule: A controlled Future Well offers Harvest, Preserve, or Reshape as mutually exclusive protocols with visible costs and no moral ranking.

factions.canon: A culturally plural governance and logistics compact whose strength comes from reliable connected infrastructure.
factions.voice_rule: Measured commitments, anchors, tolerances, ledgers, duty windows, and reserve margins.
factions.prohibited_reduction: Do not treat the Compact as a single ethnicity or as the morally correct faction.

factions.canon: A society of layered personhood, imperfectly merged ancestral memory, mobile infrastructure, and terrain adaptation.
factions.voice_rule: Present evidence may correct inherited certainty; dry humor comes from the mismatch.
factions.prohibited_reduction: Do not portray the Kharuun as primitive, mystical, or governed by infallible memory.

factions.canon: Coherent consciousness retained by erased branches; maintained possibilities carry public duration, cost, and counterplay.
factions.voice_rule: Stable speech is selected from incompatible phrasing rather than delivered as a default mystical collective voice.
factions.prohibited_reduction: Do not reveal a hidden real personality, unrestricted rewind, or cost-free complexity.

characters.arc: Disciplined preparation saves people, but her drive to make uncertainty governable can turn moral questions into control problems.
characters.continuity_boundary: Mara commands Mission 01 but is not the simulated archive-carrier entity; in Mission 10 she is an off-map liaison and in Mission 15 a protected neutral witness.

characters.arc: Oruun tests inherited memory against present evidence while confronting the accountability cost of curated communal continuity.
characters.continuity_boundary: Oruun is a Mission 01 interlocutor, becomes the Kharuun command authority in later operations, and is a protected neutral witness in Mission 15.

characters.arc: Talar preserves records that institutional ledgers omitted and insists that evidence remain attributable to the people who carried its cost.
characters.continuity_boundary: Talar requests the Mission 01 archive recovery, follows the census trail in Missions 06 and 08, and is a protected neutral witness in Mission 15.

characters.arc: Neme negotiates among internal futures that disagree about coexistence rather than revealing one secretly dominant identity.
characters.continuity_boundary: Mission 08 establishes reciprocal contact, Mission 14 a bounded local Choir command contract, and Mission 15 a final local command role; none proves a unified permanent Choir identity.

characters.arc: Rhyse argues for one governable future by pointing to cities preserved under Compact policy, at an unacceptable existential cost.
characters.continuity_boundary: Mission 12 represents Rhyse only through attributable neutral public apparatus; he is not playable or commandable.
